tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/OneParameterSemig.summary: Tau Ceti (TauCeti/Analysis/Semigroups, Normed/Operator/Resolvent, CompletelyMonotone, PositiveDefinite, Bochner) already contains essentially the whole roadmap on real Banach spaces: C₀ and contraction semigroups with generators, closedness, uniqueness, the real resolvent with its integral formula for powers and sharp power bounds, operator-norm analyticity of unbounded resolvents, bounded perturbation, both the Hille–Yosida and Lumer–Phillips theorems as iff statements, Hausdorff–Bernstein–Widder with uniqueness, Lévy–Khintchine, Bochner on finite-dimensional inner-product spaces and the Berg–Christensen–Ressel theorem; Mathlib contributes only AbsolutelyMonotoneOn, LinearPMap, charFun and Matrix.PosSemidef. Genuinely missing: uniqueness of solutions of the abstract Cauchy problem, the half-plane complex resolvent set of the complexified generator, the reciprocal complete-Bernstein/Stieltjes correspondence, and the optional LCA Bochner stretch. The roadmap's Bernstein milestone, stated with C^∞ smoothness on [0,∞), is false in the converse direction; Tau Ceti proves the correct form with continuity at 0 and complete monotonicity on (0,∞). The milestone layers repeat text from their parent parts.

targets.target: C₀ semigroup structure and contraction-semigroup subclass
targets.note: Over a real Banach space: toFun : ℝ≥0 → X →L[ℝ] X with S 0 = id, S(s+t) = S s ∘ S t and strong continuity at 0; contraction semigroups extend it with ‖S t‖ ≤ 1.

targets.note: HasGrowthBound ω M includes 1 ≤ M.

targets.target: Generator as strong derivative at 0 on its domain, as a LinearPMap
targets.note: The domain is the submodule of x for which (S t x − x)/t converges as t → 0⁺; the generator is a LinearPMap, as the roadmap requires.

targets.target: Density of D(A), and of D(Aⁿ)
targets.note: Both the named density theorem and the secondary D(Aⁿ) target are present.

The generator is closed

targets.note: The orbit derivative is within [0,∞) at every t ≥ 0 and equals A S(t)x.

targets.target: Bounded generator (domain = ⊤) iff uniformly continuous semigroup
targets.note: Continuity is of t ↦ S t in operator norm; a semigroup with bounded generator A is exp(tA).

targets.target: Bounded perturbation theorem
targets.note: For bounded B, B + A generates a C₀ semigroup with growth bound (M, ω + M‖B‖).

targets.target: ∫₀ᵗ S(s)x ds ∈ D(A) with A∫₀ᵗ S(s)x ds = S(t)x − x
Dissipativity and m-dissipativity (Banach form); generator of a contraction semigroup is m-dissipative
targets.note: Dissipativity is the resolvent-range inequality λ‖x‖ ≤ ‖λx − Ax‖ for λ > 0, the general Banach notion the roadmap asks for.

targets.target: Hilbert characterization of dissipativity ⟪Ax, x⟫ ≤ 0
targets.note: Stated for real inner product spaces, as a specialization.

targets.target: Unbounded resolvent set and resolvent, with the bridge to Mathlib's resolvent for bounded operators
targets.note: λ ∈ ρ(A) iff λI − A : D(A) → X has a bounded two-sided inverse; defined over any nontrivially normed field.

targets.target: R(λ,A)x = ∫₀^∞ e^{−λt} S(t)x dt for real λ > ω
targets.note: The Laplace integral is a pointwise Bochner integral bundled into a continuous linear map, and is identified with the abstract resolvent of the generator.

targets.target: Resolvent identity R(λ) − R(μ) = (μ − λ)R(λ)R(μ)
Analyticity of λ ↦ R(λ,A) on the resolvent set
targets.note: Proved in operator norm for any unbounded operator on a Banach space over a nontrivially normed field, so both the real resolvent set of the generator and any complex resolvent set are covered. The 2026-09-03 STATUS.md lists this as missing; it is in the baseline.

targets.note: The complexified semigroup and complex generator exist, but no theorem places the half-plane Re λ > ω in the complex resolvent set or gives the Laplace formula for complex λ.

targets.target: Derivative formula dᵏR(λ,A)/dλᵏ = (−1)ᵏ k! R(λ,A)^{k+1}
targets.note: Stated for the real resolvent function on λ > ω.

targets.target: Power formula R(λ,A)ⁿx = ∫₀^∞ tⁿ⁻¹/(n−1)! e^{−λt} S(t)x dt
targets.note: Public: `StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolvent_pow_succ_apply` states `R(λ)^(n+1) x = (1/n!) ∫_{t>0} tⁿ e^{−λt} S(t)x dt` for `λ > ω`, which is the roadmap's formula reindexed (`n ↦ n+1`); the contraction case is `ContractionSemigroup.resolvent_pow_succ_apply`. tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/FuchsianOrbifolds.summary: Layer 0 is built except the complex-analytic half of its item 5. Tau Ceti has the effective `PSL(2, R)`-action on ℍ (`UpperHalfPlane.instMulActionPSL2`), its faithfulness, joint continuity, properness, the `T2Space` on `PSL(2, ℝ)`, proper discontinuity of every discrete subgroup, and the full elliptic-stabilizer analysis — finite, cyclic, generated by an element whose derivative at the fixed point is a primitive `m`-th root of unity (`Subgroup.exists_isPrimitiveRoot_stabilizerDeriv`). The generic free-locus theory (`TauCeti.freeLocus`, `isCoveringMap_quotientMk_freeLocus`; no complex-manifold structure on the quotient, so the projection is not yet a local biholomorphism) and the finite-cyclic disc-quotient model `u ↦ u^m` (`TauCeti.rootsOfUnityBallQuotientHomeomorph`) are also built, in greater generality than the roadmap asks, and Mathlib supplies far more of the cusp layer than the roadmap assumes: the parabolic classification with its unique boundary fixed point (`IsParabolic.smul_eq_self_iff`), `IsCusp`, `CuspOrbits`, `Subgroup.strictPeriods`/`strictWidthInfty` with `strictPeriods = wℤ`, `Function.Periodic.qParam`/`cuspFunction`, and the whole removable-singularity and q-expansion chain. What is genuinely missing is everything complex-analytic about the quotient and everything polygonal: no precisely invariant horodiscs, no charted space or complex manifold on the coarse or compactified quotient, no hyperbolic polygons, Gauss--Bonnet, Poincaré polygon theorem, Dirichlet domains, triangle groups or covolume, and — the largest gap — no compact-Riemann-surface API at all, only the planar local-degree theorem and combinatorial genera (no topological genus, local multiplicity, degree, divisor pullback, degree-one biholomorphism or Riemann--Hurwitz), nor the CW Euler characteristic it is meant to be built on. The level-one application is blocked twice over: it needs those layers and it needs the `j`-function owned by ModularForms Layer 0, which exists in neither library.

targets.target: Quotient topology on PSL(2,R) with Hausdorff, second-countable topological-group structure, identified with the algebraic quotient by the centre
targets.note: `PSL(2, R)` is *by definition* Mathlib's `SL(2,R) ⧸ Subgroup.center`, so there is nothing to relate: the quotient topology, open quotient map and topological-group structure are Mathlib's generic `QuotientGroup` instances, and second countability is `QuotientGroup.instSecondCountableTopology`. Tau Ceti adds the `T2Space PSL(2, ℝ)` instance (an unnamed instance at line 29; Lean names it `TauCeti.instT2SpaceProjectiveSpecialLinearGroupFinOfNatNatReal_tauCeti`, which declarations.tsv omits), proved from finiteness of the centre.

targets.target: Canonical homomorphism PSL(2,R) → PGL(2,R) and the restricted projective Möbius action
targets.note: `toPGL` is Mathlib's; Tau Ceti builds the `PSL(2, R)`-action for every `R` with an algebra map to `ℝ` as the central-quotient descent of the `SL(2,R)`-action and proves it agrees with Mathlib's `PGL(2, ℝ)`-action along `toPGL`. No unrelated permutation action is exported.

targets.target: Compatibility of the PSL action with the SL(2,R) action on points and on sets
targets.note: `pslMk_smul` is the representative compatibility (`(↑g : PSL) • τ = g • τ`, proved by `rfl`), and well-definedness is `smul_eq_self_of_mem_center`.

targets.note: An unnamed `instance : FaithfulSMul PSL(2, ℝ) ℍ` at line 172 (auto-named `UpperHalfPlane.instFaithfulSMulProjectiveSpecialLinearGroupFinOfNatNatReal_tauCeti`, absent from declarations.tsv), obtained from Mathlib's faithful `PGL(2, ℝ)`-action along the injective `toPGL`; the corresponding `PSL(2, ℤ)` instance is at line 189.

targets.note: The unnamed `instance : ContinuousSMul PSL(2, ℝ) ℍ` at line 31, proved by pulling back along the open quotient map `SL(2,ℝ) → PSL(2,ℝ)`; this is exactly joint continuity, not merely continuity in the point.

targets.target: Every element acts by a biholomorphism of the upper half-plane
targets.note: Mathlib proves the `GL(2,ℝ)⁺` action is `MDifferentiable` on ℍ; Tau Ceti computes the nonvanishing complex derivative of the projective action. Since the action is by a group, holomorphy of `g` and of `g⁻¹` gives the biholomorphism; no single declaration packages it as an explicit `Homeomorph`/biholomorphism record.

targets.target: A discrete subgroup Γ ≤ PSL(2,R) acts properly discontinuously, related to Mathlib's SL(2,R) theorem through projective lifts
targets.note: The unnamed instance at `Fuchsian/ProperAction.lean:33` gives `ProperlyDiscontinuousSMul G ℍ` for every `G : Subgroup PSL(2, ℝ)` with `[DiscreteTopology G]`, descended from Mathlib's proper `SL(2, ℝ)`-action through the surjective quotient map — exactly the required relation to Mathlib without a chosen lift in the interface.

targets.target: Finiteness of every stabilizer, and classification of a nontrivial stabilizer as finite cyclic generated by an elliptic element
targets.note: Finiteness is Mathlib's `ProperlyDiscontinuousSMul.finite_stabilizer`, packaged by Tau Ceti as the `Finite` instance `TauCeti.finite_stabilizer_of_properlyDiscontinuousSMul` and applied through the discrete-subgroup instance; cyclicity and ellipticity of a nonidentity stabilizer element are proved outright. `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.IsElliptic` is Mathlib's discriminant definition.

targets.target: Identification of the stabilizer order with the order of the derivative in a disc coordinate
targets.note: `stabilizerDeriv` is an injective character on the stabilizer, `orderOf_stabilizerDeriv` equates orders, and `exists_isPrimitiveRoot_stabilizerDeriv` produces a generator whose derivative is a primitive `m`-th root of unity for `m = Nat.card (stabilizer Γ z)`. `discCoordinate` is the Cayley coordinate `(z - w)/(z - conj w)` centred at the fixed point, and `discCoordinate_smul_of_smul_eq_self` says a stabilizing element acts on it by multiplication by that derivative.

targets.target: The free locus {z : stabilizer Γ z = ⊥} is open and invariant
targets.note: `freeLocus G X` is defined as a `SubMulAction` (so invariance is built in) for an arbitrary group action, with openness for any properly discontinuous action on a locally compact Hausdorff space — strictly more general than the stated `Γ ≤ PSL(2,ℝ)` case, which is an instance since ℍ is locally compact Hausdorff.

targets.target: On the free locus the orbit projection is a covering map and a local biholomorphism, via the generic quotient theorem
targets.note: The covering-map and local-homeomorphism halves are fully proved generically. What is missing is the complex-analytic half: Mathlib's `instChartedSpaceQuotient` puts a `ChartedSpace ℂ` structure on a free properly discontinuous quotient but its own file records as a TODO that the quotient is not yet shown to be an `IsManifold`, and nothing states that the projection is a *local biholomorphism* (holomorphic with holomorphic local inverse) rather than a local homeomorphism.

duplicates.note: V0 asks for properly discontinuous actions of the effective quotients of arithmetic groups on symmetric spaces; the `PSL(2,ℝ)`-on-ℍ case here is its rank-one instance, and the `Γ\G/K` effective-action normalization is the same construction.

10A explicitly consumes this layer's effective action, stabilizers and quotient charts rather than restating them, so the overlap is by design; but it repeats the elliptic-order and cusp-orbit bookkeeping for congruence subgroups.

targets.target: An invariant disc at an elliptic point whose translates are disjoint outside the stabilizer
targets.note: Mathlib gives the disjointness half for any properly discontinuous action on a locally compact Hausdorff space: `ProperlyDiscontinuousSMul.exists_nhds_disjoint_image` produces a neighbourhood `U` of `x` with `γ • U` disjoint from `U` whenever `γ • x ≠ x`. Missing: a stabilizer-invariant round disc (e.g. a disc in the Cayley coordinate), the precisely-invariant packaging, and the holomorphic conjugation of the stabilizer action to multiplication by `m`-th roots of unity; no `preciselyInvariant` or horodisc notion exists in either library.

targets.target: Holomorphic linearizing coordinate conjugating the stabilizer action to the m-th roots of unity

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/OptimalTransport.summary: Layers 0--4 are largely done and sorry-free: `TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/` holds about 800 declarations covering couplings and the bundled `Coupling` space, graph plans on Mathlib's `HasLaw`, disintegration, one-sided and symmetric gluing plus Ionescu--Tulcea chains and the countable-index Kolmogorov extension theorem, multi-marginal couplings, the extended `transportCost` with a signed bounded-below interface, tightness/Prokhorov compactness, lower semicontinuity of the plan integral, primal attainment and stability, the whole `c`-transform/`c`-concave/contact-set tower with its analytic-set measurability bridge, finite and multi-marginal LP duality with both attainments and complementary slackness, strong duality on compact metrizable spaces (continuous and lower-semicontinuous costs), dual certificates, and a `W_p` theory for all `p ∈ [1,∞]` with the triangle inequality by gluing, completeness, separability, density of finite support and quantization convergence. Mathlib contributes `klDiv` with its chain rule and data-processing inequality, the realization of every standard-Borel law by a map from the unit interval, Arzelà–Ascoli, metric absolutely continuous curves, the Brownian-motion predicates, `GromovHausdorff.ghDist`, `levyProkhorovEDist`, `ConvexOn.locallyLipschitzOn_interior` and Rademacher. The roadmap names some of these as inputs, but asks to prove data processing and the deterministic Arzelà–Ascoli theorem, which Mathlib already has. From Layer 5 on, only the Gaussian matrix toolkit exists (Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.geometricMean`, the unique positive solution of `A S A = T`, and the affine Gaussian pushforward); everything else is missing. There is no Legendre--Fenchel conjugate anywhere in either library, hence no Brenier theorem, no Monge--Ampère measure or regularity theory, no Riemannian exponential map (so no McCann), no `ACᵖ` curves for `p > 1`, continuity equation or Benamou--Brenier, no displacement convexity, no metric gradient flows, EVI, JKO or Γ-convergence, no Boltzmann entropy functional, no Fréchet or Wasserstein barycenters, no entropic transport or Sinkhorn, no CD/RCD theory, and no Gromov--Wasserstein. Within Layers 0--4 the notable residual gaps are the Polish lower-semicontinuous duality theorem, dual attainment under a split upper envelope, the Schachermayer--Teichmann converse (flagged in Tau Ceti's own docstring), Kantorovich--Rubinstein for `W₁`, Pratelli's Monge=Kantorovich theorem, the `W_p`-convergence characterization, the Borel σ-algebra of `P_p(X)`, `W_∞` attainment and completeness, and two acceptance checks (matrix gluing versus measure gluing, and optimality of the monotone coupling).

AnalyticNumberTheory.summary: The first two stages are essentially finished in the libraries, which the roadmap document does not reflect. Mathlib supplies the whole `LSeries` carrier with abscissa of absolute convergence, termwise differentiation, Euler products, Abel summation, Mellin transform and inversion; `riemannZeta` with its completed form, functional equation, residue at 1 and trivial zeros; Dirichlet L-functions with gamma factors, completed L-functions, root numbers, the primitive functional equation, change of level for imprimitive characters, and nonvanishing on `Re s ≥ 1`; Hurwitz and periodic (exponential) zeta with continuation, residue, Hurwitz's functional equation and Bernoulli special values; Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions; Chebyshev's `ψ` and `θ` with Chebyshev's bounds, `ψ − θ = O(√x)` and the exact identity converting `θ` to `π`; `dedekindZeta` together with a proved **Dirichlet class number formula**; and Dirichlet density for sets of prime ideals. Tau Ceti adds the ideal-indexed Dirichlet-series library (`ArithmeticDirichletSeries`, ~665 declarations) with Perron inversion and explicit truncation errors, Landau's theorem, ψ and θ for prime ideals with the transfer `ϑ ∼ δx ⇒ π ∼ δ Li(x)`, and a partial Wiener--Ikehara and Chebotarev development. What is genuinely missing is the quantitative half of the subject: no zero-free region of positive width, no Tauberian theorem in final form, no prime number theorem (in any shape) and no PNT in progressions, no zero-counting or explicit formula, no zero-density or mean-value estimates, no continuation or functional equation for Dedekind zeta, no Hecke or Artin L-functions, and almost nothing from AN.5, AN.8 and AN.9: no multiplicative-function mean values, Halász, moments, prehomogeneous or multiple zeta functions, Selberg zeta or Bost--Connes, only Mathlib's elementary bound on the smooth-number count.

review.notes: All 351 targets and all 679 citations were checked against the pinned baseline. 672 citations match declarations.tsv at the exact file and line. In the other 7 the name field was not a declaration name (4 unnamed instances, 3 'TauCeti.fourierAtom (public def …)'); all are fixed, and Lean confirms the names and lines. No cited file contains a sorry token or declares an axiom. The statements of all cited declarations were read against their targets. Every declaration newly cited or named in a corrected note was checked in Lean: 43 names, against the pinned Mathlib and a build whose Tau Ceti sources are byte-identical to the pin, with axioms only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Every built and process verdict was checked against the layer text. All 213 absent and partial claims were searched again by concept, Mathlib naming convention and keyword, over the index and both source trees. Target status changes (9): absent to partial for FuchsianOrbifolds L1 T0, OptimalTransport L3 T5 and L8 T1; partial to present for OneParameterSemigroups A T18, AnalyticNumberTheory AN.2 T5 and OptimalTransport L5 T2; present to partial for OptimalTransport L0 T7, L2 T5 and L3 T2. Verdict changes (4): FuchsianOrbifolds L0 and OptimalTransport L0 and L1 go from built to partly built (the first two had listed a partial target of their own), and OptimalTransport L5 from not built to partly built. Library content wrongly reported absent: Mathlib's Chebyshev ψ/θ/π file; the KL chain rule and data processing; the unit-interval realization of standard-Borel laws; Arzelà–Ascoli; metric absolutely continuous curves; the parabolic fixed point; the smooth-number count bound. On the Tau Ceti side: the public resolvent-power formula, the matrix geometric mean, the countable Kolmogorov extension, the empirical-measure law and a Monge-feasibility realization. Presence overstated: Kantorovich duality is only compact, not Polish; W_∞ attainment and completeness hold only for finite p. Private declarations cited as exact were replaced by public ones where a public equivalent exists. Four private citations remain, each documenting how a result is proved rather than exporting it: the Bochner existence route, the Rockafellar potential, the roots-of-unity quotient map and a few 'related' helpers. 12 duplicate records were added and two ModularForms ownership notes corrected. All 53 duplicate records point at existing layers of unretired roadmaps.
